title: Gemini in Android Auto could finally keep my hands off my phone at red lights
excerpt: Nobody needs Gemini to book a table from their phone, but behind the wheel, it's genius
content_html:
Published Nov 16, 2026, 11:00 AM EST

If you've ever wondered whether an AI feature on your phone is doing anything useful, Ben Khalesi has probably asked the same question. He has covered AI and Android for Android Police since 2023, with Pixel, Galaxy, Google's apps, and the rest of the Android ecosystem never far behind. Ben is a lifelong geek who trained as an AI engineer and earned a bachelor's in IT, so when the industry announces something new, he's the one who wants to know how everything works behind the scene and what can be trusted.

Booking a dinner reservation on my phone takes a few taps. I open the app, pick a time, and I'm done.

Asking Gemini to do the same thing is, let's be real here, unnecessary.

I have to say the prompt out loud and wait while the request travels to Google's servers and back.

Taps are faster, and I can see what I'm agreeing to. Unless you're behind the wheel. That's when the story changes.

In the car, the same slow voice that tests my patience every day becomes the safest tool I have. And boy, am I glad Google keeps giving it more to do.

What I want next is for Gemini in Android Auto to reach the apps I use every day, and Google has started building the system that could make that happen.

Voice commands make more sense in the car

Eyes on the road, please

Voice commands are faster than a touchscreen for complicated tasks only when you can't safely look at or touch a screen.

In a moving car, keeping your eyes on the road and your hands on the wheel is non-negotiable.

Picking up a phone to check a reservation or to track a package takes your eyes and hands off the job and drags your attention along with them.

Voice controls cut out the visual and manual distractions that make phone use behind the wheel dangerous.

That's a job an AI agent can do well. I say what I want once, and my agent handles the steps I'd otherwise tap through.

Gemini in Android Auto already covers the basics

Personal Intelligence digs through Gmail so you don't

Google has replaced the old Google Assistant with Gemini in its car software. On October 20, 2026, it started rolling out Personal Intelligence for Android Auto.

The feature lets the in-car assistant pull from your personal data across Google Workspace, Maps, Photos, and even YouTube. It's optional. You have to switch it on yourself.

After it's on, you can ask questions that depend on personal context without taking your hands off the wheel.

Heading to the airport? Ask for your gate number and whether your flight is delayed. Gemini pulls the booking from your Gmail confirmation and checks live flight data to answer both.

You can also do other cool tricks, like asking for an indoor restaurant along your route that matches your usual vibe.

Gemini factors in what it knows about you when it narrows down the results. If you're vegetarian, chances are, Gemini already knows. So the shortlist fits without you having to say it.

Notice a pattern? Every app on that list belongs to Google. It's a closed loop. Every answer comes from an app Google owns, so Gemini finds the restaurant and that's the end of the road.

The fix is to let apps like OpenTable plug into Gemini everywhere, including the dashboard.

Google now has a platform built to do that, but the car isn't on its list yet. Still, I can't think of a good reason it won't get there soon.

Connected Apps could give the car its missing piece

The platform is still a developer preview

On October 28, 2026, Google announced the Connected Apps Platform as a developer preview. It gives outside developers an official way to plug their app's features into Gemini.

The first phase is a beta for US developers, who have to apply through a waitlist. So no, every app isn't getting wired into Gemini overnight.

That's the plumbing AI agents need. Again, Google hasn't mentioned Android Auto or any in-car surface for the platform yet.

But Google said it will open the platform to more of its products over the coming months. Android Auto runs from your phone, which is why I'm optimistic and think the car is the next stop.

My wish list for Gemini on the drive

None of this works in Android Auto today. But let's imagine, shall we?

Say I'm stuck in traffic on the way to dinner. I'd ask Gemini to push my 7 p.m. table to 7:30 on OpenTable and text my friend the new time.

On the drive home, I'd ask Gemini to add eggs and oat milk to my Instacart cart.

When my dentist's office calls to reschedule, I'd ask Gemini to find an open Thursday morning slot on Zocdoc and read me the options.

When I'm 10 minutes from home, I'd have Gemini turn on the hallway lights and get the heat going.

None of these apps were built to talk to each other. Gemini could be the glue that connects them, and all I'd have to do is ask.
